macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rebound as oil retreats after Iran-related shock
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as global markets and oil prices steadied after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran renewed geopolitical anxiety. Reuters said investors were balancing the conflict risk against signs that oil had retreated from earlier highs.

items.title: European shares gain as tech stocks recover in choppy trading
items.summary: European equities rose in volatile trade, led by a rebound in technology shares. Reuters said investors were still focused on the Middle East conflict and its implications for energy prices and risk sentiment.

items.title: Asian shares rise, but oil-driven inflation fears cap gains
items.summary: Asian markets climbed as semiconductors stabilized after heavy selling, though gains were limited by a surge in oil prices. Reuters reported that renewed fighting in the Gulf raised inflation concerns and weighed on bonds.

items.title: Japan 10-year government bond yield hits 30-year high
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year Japanese Government Bond yield reached a 30-year high as rising oil prices revived inflation worries and investors remained uneasy about Japan’s fiscal position. Reuters said the move reflected broader global rate and inflation pressure.

items.title: India inflation likely moved above the RBI’s 4% target
items.summary: A Reuters poll found India’s consumer inflation likely breached the central bank’s medium-term target for the first time in 16 months in June. The poll cited higher food and fuel prices, the U.S.-Iran war, and a weak monsoon as key drivers.

items.title: China producer inflation jumps to near 4-year high
items.summary: China’s producer prices rose at the fastest pace since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased, signaling persistent cost pressure for manufacturers. Reuters reported the data as evidence that domestic inflationary pressures remain elevated.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast on Iran-war fallout
items.summary: The IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast to 3%, citing the economic impact of the Iran conflict. Al Jazeera said the fund also noted that AI-related demand is partially offsetting the energy shock.

items.title: U.S. trade deficit surges amid AI spending boom
items.summary: The U.S. trade deficit widened sharply to $77.6 billion in May as imports outpaced exports. Al Jazeera said the increase was driven by pharmaceuticals and semiconductors amid an artificial intelligence spending boom.

items.title: Some Fed officials still saw need for future rate rises
items.summary: Financial Times reported that minutes from the latest Federal Reserve meeting showed some officials remained concerned about persistent inflation and saw a need for further rate increases. The report suggested the Fed is still weighing inflation risks despite slower growth.

items.title: Taiwan central bank warns AI boom could become a bubble
items.summary: The governor of Taiwan’s central bank said the growth behind the AI boom is real, but so are the risks of an AI bubble. Reuters reported the comments amid continued volatility in global technology shares.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major crypto assets trade lower after a broader market selloff
items.summary: CoinDesk reported Bitcoin down 5.7% in its latest index update, with Bitcoin Cash also falling 4.8% and Polkadot dropping 11% below key support at $2.05. CryptoSlate’s market snapshot showed Bitcoin at $63,249.72, Ethereum at $1,746.80, XRP at $1.10, and Solana at $78.07, all reflecting a mixed-to-soft market tone over 24 hours.

items.title: Europol dismantles Bitcoin-mixing service used by ransomware and darknet actors
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that European authorities seized the crypto-mixing platform Cryptomixer, taking servers, data, and about $29 million in Bitcoin while estimating the service laundered more than $1.51 billion in BTC. The operation is one of the most significant enforcement actions in the past day.

items.title: Canada moves toward stablecoin rules as regulators focus on payments modernization
items.summary: CoinDesk said Canada is considering a stablecoin framework, with Scotiabank describing the effort as mainly aimed at modernizing payments rather than reshaping broader financial markets. The development signals continued regulatory attention on dollar-linked crypto assets.

items.title: Gleec buys Komodo’s cross-chain DeFi stack in $23.5 million deal
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that Gleec acquired Komodo’s atomic-swap technology, token ecosystem, and core developers in a $23.5 million transaction. The deal is a notable infrastructure and project-development move in blockchain interoperability.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $63K as easing oil prices support risk appetite
items.summary: crypto.news reported Bitcoin rising above $63,000, citing improved risk sentiment from softer oil prices. The same coverage highlighted related market attention around Ethereum Foundation AI research, U.S. CLARITY Act politics, and XRP-linked payment developments.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform authentication requirements
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission is forcing crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication, a regulatory move aimed at strengthening security standards. The change is part of a wider regional push for tighter oversight of exchanges.

items.title: PayPal expands PYUSD to Polygon’s Open Money Stack
items.summary: crypto.news said PayPal is bringing its PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack, adding another blockchain integration for the payment token. The move is a notable project-development story for stablecoin adoption and payments infrastructure.

items.title: XRP gains attention as SWIFT taps Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments
items.summary: crypto.news reported XRP price strength alongside news that SWIFT is working with Ripple-linked banks on blockchain-based payments. The story suggests continued institutional and cross-border payments interest around the XRP ecosystem.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent in ChatGPT designed to execute tasks across applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. Reuters also reported related OpenAI product activity, including a new real-time voice model family and broader workplace-focused features.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 to developers
items.summary: Meta opened developer access to Muse Spark 1.1 in a public API preview, positioning the model against Anthropic and OpenAI in the paid enterprise AI market. The release was described as an upgrade over the first generation with stronger coding capabilities.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. Reuters said the models are aimed at more natural conversational experiences.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, which it called its most intelligent model to date, with a focus on coding and agentic tasks. The release underscores continued competition among frontier model developers.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body responsible for keeping the company aligned with its public mission. The move reflects ongoing governance and safety positioning among leading AI firms.

items.title: New York Times-led group seeks sanctions against OpenAI in copyright case
items.summary: A group of newspapers led by the New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging the company misrepresented its ability to search systems for evidence in the copyright dispute. The filing escalates a closely watched legal battle over AI training data.

items.title: Meta announces new AI data center in Alberta
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand compute capacity for AI. The project highlights continued infrastructure investment across the AI industry.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner for data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the U.S.-based owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for violations of data protection rules. The case adds to growing regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI products.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony says PS5 physical game production will end in January 2028
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment clarified that it plans to stop producing physical game discs for new PS5 titles in January 2028, making future releases digital-only at retail and through the PlayStation Store.

items.title: Bethesda confirms Oblivion Remastered is coming to Switch 2 on August 11, 2026
items.summary: Bethesda Softworks has confirmed a Switch 2 release date for The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered, giving the long-awaited remaster a new launch platform and date.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games has reached a settlement with former contractor Hayden Cohen in a case over alleged leaks of confidential Fortnite collaboration information, dropping its monetary claims.

items.title: Microsoft increases investment in MachineGames, according to insider report
items.summary: A report says Microsoft is significantly increasing its investment in MachineGames following the commercial success of Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and continued interest in Wolfenstein.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 is set to become a standalone launcher title
items.summary: A report says Black Ops 6 will move to its own dedicated launcher on July 7, separating it from the unified Call of Duty HQ hub.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced launches
items.summary: GamingBolt reports that Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is out now, with a launch trailer reviving the fan-favorite 2013 game.

items.title: Game Kitchen teases a key date for Ninja Gaiden fans
items.summary: During Sony’s State of Play showcase, The Game Kitchen revealed an important upcoming date for Ninja Gaiden fans, suggesting more news tied to the franchise.

items.title: Helldivers 2 reveals the Force of Law Warbond
items.summary: Arrowhead’s co-op shooter is getting a new Force of Law Warbond, expanding its live-service content with fresh unlocks for players.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some smartphone and electronics parts
items.summary: India removed import duties on certain components used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion in chip-supply deal with Broadcom
items.summary: Apple plans to invest more than $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom, which will also expand a factory in Colorado. The deal underscores Apple’s continued push to secure critical semiconductor supply.

items.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in record U.S. market debut by a foreign company
items.summary: SK Hynix completed the largest-ever U.S. market debut by a foreign company, selling 177.9 million ADRs for $149 each. The offering was more than seven times oversubscribed.

items.title: European startups raise $24 billion in Q2, strongest quarter in four years
items.summary: European startups raised $24 billion in the second quarter, up 66% year over year and the strongest quarterly total in four years. The U.K. led the region with $10.4 billion raised.

items.title: SAP moves to avert EU antitrust fine by easing contract switching
items.summary: SAP will make it easier for customers to switch to rival providers or end contracts, according to reports, in a move aimed at avoiding a possible EU antitrust fine after a probe launched in September 2025.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: An internal memo reviewed by Reuters says Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September. The company is also targeting 14 gigawatts of overall computing power next year.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules to let platforms remove child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed a proposal to reinstate temporary rules allowing platforms such as Google and Meta to detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The measure is intended to bridge a legal gap while longer-term rules are pursued.

items.title: US SEC settlement with Elon Musk over Twitter purchase approved by federal judge
items.summary: A federal judge approved the SEC’s settlement with Elon Musk over his purchase of Twitter shares, despite expressing significant misgivings about the agreement. The ruling removes a major legal uncertainty tied to the deal.
